criteria.rationale: Verified timeout measurement precedes state.mu.Lock in both capture paths. Verified existing WithoutCancel semantics rather than assuming caller cancellation bounds the final audit. The spec explicitly acknowledges cumulative replay latency. The reported 135-second index run was not independently reproduced; approval rests on source inspection and sealed regression evidence.

Examined the diff and production callers. No exported signatures, CLI/MCP schemas, stored formats, or output contracts change. Reads without deadlines retain their existing behavior; deadline-bound audit replays receive a fresh duration.

D1 addresses R1-R3 directly: auditTimeout computes deadline minus capture start with a positive fallback, and both replay sites use WithTimeout. This removes dependence on an expired absolute instant while retaining per-read bounds. Timeout capture occurs before state-lock queuing; existing synchronization and comparison logic remain intact. No individual structural delta facts were enumerated in the brief.

Compared the scope spec, D1, requirement trace, code comments and registered test command against runtime behavior. They describe fresh per-read audit timeouts, the positive expired-deadline fallback and cumulative audit latency consistently. No public operational interface requires migration.

Examined replay failures and budget-exhaustion handling. Existing changed/unknown producer reporting, bounded diagnostic summaries and hashed Git identifiers remain intact. Unchanged successful reads no longer produce false changes solely because their original deadline passed.

Compared the declared implementation artifacts with the scoped diff. Changes are confined to recording and replaying timeout durations, focused regression coverage and its required validation registration. Generated governance material is distinguished from implementation changes.

Inspected context construction, command arguments, root routing, retained observations and audit budgets. Every previously deadline-bound replay remains deadline-bound. The change adds no command interpolation, dependency, authority expansion, sensitive diagnostic content or budget bypass.

The shared duration helper plus one duration field per observation and two replay substitutions are sufficient for D1. Increasing original deadlines merely postpones recurrence; removing deadlines loses the bound. No scheduler, global timeout policy or speculative abstraction is added. A future requirement that caller cancellation or one absolute deadline bound the entire audit would require reconsidering this design; the existing detached audit contract does not impose that requirement.
